deck.audience: ML researchers, on-device AI engineers, and graduate students working on efficient multimodal models

brief.title: SmolVLM: Redefining Small and Efficient Multimodal Models
brief.one_liner: SmolVLM is a family of compact vision-language models that achieve competitive performance with dramatically lower memory footprints through strategic architectural optimizations.
brief.goal: Understand SmolVLM's key design decisions — compute allocation, token compression, and training data curation — and how they enable sub-1GB inference for multimodal tasks on edge devices.

slides.title: SmolVLM: Redefining Small and Efficient Multimodal Models
slides.objective: Cover slide with paper title, authors (Hugging Face & Stanford), and a key visual showing the SmolVLM architecture or logo. Set the context of efficient on-device VLMs.

slides.title: Large VLMs Are Powerful but Impractical for Edge Deployment
slides.objective: Frame the problem: state-of-the-art VLMs require massive compute and memory, limiting mobile/edge use. Contrast parameter counts and RAM usage of existing models. Use a concise bullet list or comparison graphic.

slides.title: SmolVLM Architecture: Image Splitting, Pixel Shuffle, and SmolLM2 Backbone
slides.objective: Show the SmolVLM architecture pipeline diagram (image splitting → vision encoder → pixel shuffle → linear projection → SmolLM2). Reference the architecture figure. Explain the flow in 3-4 key steps.

slides.title: Smaller Vision Encoders Outperform Larger Ones in Compact VLMs
slides.objective: Present Finding 1: balanced encoder-LM parameter allocation matters. Show how a 93M SigLIP-B/16 outperforms the 428M SigLIP-SO400M for the smallest LMs. Use a bar chart or comparison visual referencing the experimental results.

slides.title: Aggressive Pixel Shuffle (r=4) Cuts Visual Tokens 16× for Small Models
slides.objective: Explain pixel shuffle and its impact on token count. Show that small VLMs benefit from r=4 compression while larger models prefer r=2. Include the pixel shuffle diagram and performance comparison across shuffle factors.

slides.title: Extending Context from 2K to 16K Tokens Unlocks Higher Image Resolution
slides.objective: Present Finding 2: performance improves significantly with extended context length from 2K to 16K tokens. Explain the RoPE base adjustment from 10K to 273K and fine-tuning on mixed long/short-context data. Note that the 2.2B model uses 16K context while smaller variants use 8K. Use a concise bullet list or diagram to illustrate the context extension strategy and its qualitative impact.

slides.title: SmolVLM Achieves Competitive Performance at Sub-1GB to 4.9GB RAM
slides.objective: Present the full benchmark comparison table across Single-Image, Multi-task, and Video benchmarks for SmolVLM 256M/500M/2.2B vs. Best Efficient OS baselines (Molmo-A1B-7B, InternVL2-2B). Highlight the average scores (44.0%, 51.0%, 59.8%) and RAM usage (0.8GB to 4.9GB vs. 27.7GB for Molmo-A1B-7B). Note that SmolVLM-256M surpasses the 300× larger Idefics-80B per the paper's key findings. Use a data table visualization.

slides.title: Real-Time Inference on iPhones: Up to 80 Tokens/Second on Apple Silicon
slides.objective: Show on-device deployment results: HuggingSnap mobile app screenshots and throughput charts across Apple Silicon devices. Highlight tokens-per-second at different model sizes and batch sizes. Reference the performance graphs.

slides.title: Key Takeaways: Design Principles for Efficient Multimodal Models
slides.objective: Summarize 4-5 actionable findings: (1) balance encoder-LM compute, (2) extend context length, (3) use aggressive token compression for small models, (4) sub-1GB inference is achievable, (5) fully open-source release. End with implications for on-device AI.
